A. Output: Feature Roadmap Document
What was delivered:
The full Onboard.Ninja feature roadmap is published as a public GitHub Project. Every item on it is tagged with a Phase (Public Beta, Public Launch, Post Launch, or Future Development) and a Status from the five options listed in the milestone brief (Complete, Testing, Development, Roadmap, Proposed). Features critical to Public Beta and Public Launch are grouped together in the summary below so they're easy to pick out.
Acceptance criteria:
Feature roadmap is publicly published, every feature has one of the five required statuses, and every feature has a development phase assigned with an estimated completion window.
Evidence:
・Public roadmap: https://github.com/orgs/cardano-onboard/projects/2
・Feature summary by status and phase:
・Complete, Public Beta (03/2026): campaign create + detail view, user registration, user login, user dashboard, consumers can successfully claim codes.
・Testing, Public Beta (03/2026): edit campaign details (with field locking once claims exist), refund bucket contents to a specified address, transaction status re-check with retry, security hardening (22 fixes), automated test suite (76 tests / 141 assertions), CI/CD test gate, self-hosted Docker support, brand refresh, env-configurable rate and upload limits, Bech32 address validation (BIP-173 / CIP-19).
・Development, Public Launch (Q3 2026): campaign list improvements, top up campaign bucket via a connected wallet.
・Roadmap, Public Launch (Q3 2026): charts and reports on campaign performance, code reward details, bulk code generation, download-all QR codes, import known native assets from public sources.
・Testing, ahead of schedule (originally slated for Post Launch Q4 2026): NMKR API integration for NFT distribution, TransactionBackend interface (so Phyrhose is swappable for self-hosters).
・Proposed, Post Launch (Q4 2026): filter codes by claimed/unclaimed, send a random amount of tokens within a range, dashboard pagination, dashb

All seven launch-critical features are now Complete on the public roadmap: four landed in Milestone 2, and the final three shipped this milestone — campaign performance charts/reports, per-code reward details (Koios-enriched token names and decimals), and known-native-asset import by ticker (a cache-backed token registry). ms.report:
A. Output: Evidence of continued development progress, including feature roadmap status updates, issues and bug reports addressed, and pull requests and release version iteration. Four post-launch features shipped this milestone and are publicly released as v1.3.0-beta: built-in onboarding analysis, which measures for every claimant wallet whether it existed before the claim, whether it has initiated a transaction of its own since, and whether it is delegated to a stake pool; code deletion, individually, as a selection, or every unclaimed code in a campaign, with claimed codes protected because their claims are the payment record; claimed-address export to CSV carrying the onboarding classification; and dashboard search with a small-screen layout. Twenty-two roadmap items that were complete in the product but still open as issues were verified against the running code and closed, each with a comment naming what implements it. Two launch-relevant items remain in progress and are recorded on the roadmap: transaction independence when self-hosting, and moving QR export to a queued job. Separately, on the public platform repository, five security and hardening issues filed during Milestone 2 were verified as implemented and closed, and eight hardening and testing items remain open. Test suite: 258 PHPUnit (671 assertions) and 73 Vitest passing, up from 209 and 54 at the previous milestone, gating every pull request into the release branches.
Acceptance criteria: The reviewer can confirm post-launch feature development and refinement aligned with the project development roadmap, via the roadmap board, the closed issues, the public release tag, and the development activity summary.
